title: Kibeho (Rwanda)
hook: visions in the 1980s that were later read as warnings before the genocide

segments.voice: Yesterday, Knock: a vision in the Irish rain where no one said a word. Your line was the silent apparition.

Nyina wa Jambo. In Kinyarwanda, the language of Rwanda, that means Mother of the Word. It's the name schoolgirls at a boarding school in the village of Kibeho said a lady gave herself when she appeared to them. Their classmates mocked them. Teachers doubted them. Crowds came to watch them in their visions, some believers, others not. And among the things the young women described were scenes so dark that, years later, people in Rwanda looked back at them and shivered.
screen: `NYINA WA JAMBO.` → `SCHOOLGIRLS, DOUBTED AND MOCKED.` → `SCENES PEOPLE LATER LOOKED BACK AT.`

segments.voice: Begin with the name. Mother of the Word points to the opening of John's Gospel, where the Word is with God in the beginning, and then, in the Douay-Rheims, "the Word was made flesh, and dwelt among us." To call Mary Mother of the Word is to say who she is entirely through her son. Then the message. By the young women's accounts, the lady asked for prayer and conversion, for hearts turned back to God before it was too late. She asked them to pray the rosary of the Seven Sorrows, which walks through Mary's griefs. Then the darkness. In one vision, by the accounts, they saw terrible things: rivers of blood, people killing one another, bodies left unburied. They wept as they described it. Later, Rwanda went through the genocide against the Tutsi, and Kibeho itself became a place of killing. Afterward, people came to read those visions as warnings that had come before. No one is required to read them that way; it's a reading made looking back. The Church studied the visions carefully and recognized some of them. Last, the sorrow. Kibeho today has a shrine to Our Lady of Sorrows, a place of pilgrimage and of mourning. Matthew's Gospel, telling of children killed in Bethlehem, borrows a prophet's line: "Rachel bewailing her children, and would not be comforted, because they are not." The Gospel doesn't explain that grief away, and a shrine of sorrows doesn't either.
screen: `MOTHER OF THE WORD.` · `PRAY, AND TURN BACK.` · `VISIONS READ AS WARNINGS.` · `A SHRINE OF SORROWS.` · then, large: `THE WORD WAS MADE FLESH.`

segments.voice: Hold Rwanda in mind, its hills, its villages, its people today, and then the ones who survived and still carry what they lost, the ones working slowly to live beside neighbors again, the ones never mourned by name. Don't hurry past the heaviness. If you pray, say a Hail Mary for Rwanda or pray one of the Seven Sorrows; if not, simply hold its people gently. And if this stirs a grief too heavy to hold, or you don't want to be alive, please call or text 988 in the US, or reach local emergency help.
Kibeho. The village in Rwanda where schoolgirls said Mary called herself Mother of the Word and asked for prayer, in visions later read as warnings. Today's word.
Your line: mother of the word. She is named entirely through her son. Until tomorrow.

howItsDone: Catholics honor Our Lady of Kibeho at the Shrine of Our Lady of Sorrows in Kibeho, Rwanda, where pilgrims pray, often using the rosary of the Seven Sorrows the visionaries said Mary asked for, and remember those killed in the genocide.

chat.says: Does the Church say the Kibeho visions predicted the genocide in Rwanda?
options: Some read them as warnings, looking back; no one is required to, though some visions were recognized.
Yes. Recognizing the visions means Catholics must believe they foretold the genocide exactly.
No. The Church rejected every one of the visions, so the shrine there honors only the dead.
chat.meaning: People read the dark visions as warnings only looking back. The Church recognized some visions, but no one is required to read them that way.

No dates or numbers are given in the voice (the index hook's '1980s' is not spoken). The bishop of Gikongoro (Augustin Misago) recognized the apparitions to three visionaries (Alphonsine Mumureke, Nathalie Mukamazimpaka, Marie Claire Mukangango); the script says 'recognized some of them'. Confirm.
'Nyina wa Jambo' as Mother of the Word in Kinyarwanda: confirm spelling and translation.
The dark vision (rivers of blood, people killing one another, bodies left unburied) is paraphrased from accounts of the visions; confirm.
'Afterward, people came to read those visions as warnings': 'many' is a general claim; consider 'people came to read'.

History handled carefully: 'the genocide against the Tutsi', and Kibeho 'became a place of killing' (massacres at the Kibeho parish and the Kibeho camp). Confirm the wording is accurate and appropriately restrained.
Shrine named Our Lady of Sorrows; the rosary (chaplet) of the Seven Sorrows. Confirm.
'Some Catholics in Rwanda speak of a mother who stood by them' is a general statement; confirm or soften.
